title: Enterprise compliance questions and stakeholder maps for private deployments
content:
Purpose: A compact playbook for sales, solutions engineering, and GTM leads to navigate early-stage compliance conversations about private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. This doc bundles: 1) a stakeholder map with the most common red flags each buyer role raises, 2) a prioritized Q&A bank for rapid replies, 3) short control-plane language that engineers and security leaders can accept, and 4) competitive signals to watch during negotiation. Use this as a live cheat sheet during calls and in pre-meeting prep.

High-level positioning guidance (one-liners to adapt by audience):
- For Security/Compliance: "You retain custody of keys, full auditability of request/response flows, and an option for an isolated control plane — we orchestrate, you own the record."
- For Platform/Infra: "Same API surface and tooling as hosted, but deployable inside your VPC — we provide a small operator footprint and automation hooks for infra teams."
- For Procurement/Legal: "We offer clear SLAs for Dedicated, contract terms for Private deployments, and a documented attestations package for audits."

Stakeholder map and rapid rebuttals
- CISO / Head of Security
  Typical concerns: data exfiltration, third-party access to plaintext, key compromise, auditability, incident response boundaries.
  Quick rebuttals (talking points):
  - Custody and keys: "Customer-managed KMS or HSM integration is supported; cloud KMS + BYOK patterns are standard."
  - Third-party access: "Control plane can be configured to run in customer VPC or under a minimal managed control plane with role-based access and attested boundary logs."
  - Auditability: "We ship structured audit logs compatible with SIEMs, include immutable request/response hashes, and can increase retention for compliance packages."
  - Incident playbooks: "We co-author an incident response runbook with on-call handoffs and can commit to joint tabletop cadence in SOW."

- Privacy / Data Protection Officer
  Typical concerns: data residency, data subject rights, deletion guarantees.
  Quick rebuttals:
  - Residency: "Models and inference can be pinned to specified regions or on-prem nodes; control plane metadata residency options are documented."
  - Deletion: "We support schema-driven soft and hard delete workflows and provide attestations for erasure where supported by infra."

- Platform or Cloud Engineering
  Typical concerns: operational blast radius, automation complexity, observability integration.
  Quick rebuttals:
  - Automation: "Opinionated Terraform modules and Helm charts for private control plane; we provide example pipelines for CI/CD and upgrade rollouts."
  - Observability: "Exporters for Prometheus, structured traces, and token-level billing hooks for cost attribution."

- Legal / Procurement
  Typical concerns: indemnity, SLA credits, data processing agreements.
  Quick rebuttals:
  - Contracts: "We offer standard DPA and can include SOC2/ISO attestation addenda; dedicated deployments get explicit uptime SLAs aligned to resource commitments."
  - Liability: "For private installs we operate under a professional services/enterprise license framework with mutually agreed responsibilities in SOWs."

Prioritized objection bank (framing + short reply)
- "We can't risk vendor access to model inputs/outputs."
  Reply: "We provide customer-managed key options and the ability to host the control plane in your VPC or on-prem so that persisted inputs/outputs never transit a vendor-managed store."

- "On-prem takes too long to stand up/risky upgrades."
  Reply: "We offer a compact operator footprint with automated migration tooling, and a canary rollout pattern so upgrades can be validated on a small subset of capacity before cross-site promotion."

- "We already built an in-house inference layer; why switch?"
  Reply: "We focus on production economics — continuous batching, KV cache reuse, quantization-aware kernels, and cost-transparent knobs that reduce unit token spend while preserving latency. We can integrate with existing model artifacts and replace only the serving layer to reduce migration risk."

Control plane language for technical docs (copyable snippets)
- Minimal-managed control plane: "Redwood ships a control plane component that can be deployed in a customer VPC. The control plane stores metadata and routing policies only; no model keys or plaintext inputs are persisted by default. Customers integrate with their KMS for key material, and all control-plane actions are logged to a customer-managed audit sink."

- Customer-managed control plane (on-prem): "Full control plane deployment owned by the customer. Redwood provides operator tooling and maintenance runbooks. Network endpoints are configured to be internal-only; the customer is responsible for host-level security and HSM/KMS integration per their policies."

Competitive signals map (what to watch in deals)
- Signals a competitor is positioning against us as purely self-hosted: they will over-index on "no vendor contact" and sell minimal observability. Counter: emphasize our hybrid controls, attestation docs, and co-managed upgrade windows.
- Signals a vendor is pushing hosted convenience: they will promise faster onboarding but avoid strong contractual isolation. Counter: push the risk profile and auditability requirements and show a timeline for Private deployment pilots with SOW milestones.

Negotiation levers (what we can concede vs what to hold)
- Concede: increased log retention for audit windows, an explicit upgrade freeze period, dedicated onboarding/resourcing in SOW.
- Hold: core responsibility split (who has admin keys), baseline SLA language tied to committed capacity, indemnity caps for infra not in our control.

Pre-call checklist for AE / SE
- Who will attend from the customer? Map roles to our talking points.
- Bring the matching artifact: attestation pack, sample SOW, operator manifest, SOC2 packet.
- Prepare a pilot plan: 6–8 week timeline, success criteria (latency SLO, cost per 1M tokens, audit logs validated), and rollback criteria.

Attachments / annex (technical items to surface quickly)
- KMS/HSM patterns: BYOK via cloud KMS, KMIP-compatible HSM adapter, and optional enclave-based key wrapping.
- Audit artifacts: example log schema, recommended SIEM ingestion mapping, sample retention policy language.
- FedRAMP / regional requirements: checklist (data residency, personnel access, background checks) to use as a rapid qualification filter.

Next actions / open items
- SEs: draft a 1-page ‘‘control plane technical brief’’ to hand to infra teams (owner: Marco Ruiz, due: 2026-03-17).
- Legal: prepare a short DPA addendum template for private installs that lists retention/erasure commitments (owner: Sofia Jensen, due: 2026-03-24).
- GTM: run two deal rehearsals with real scenarios (buyer: CISO-first and procurement-first) and capture new objections (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-04-01).

Notes on tone and risk framing
- Avoid absolute statements like "no-one can access" without qualifying operational controls. Use "customer-managed" and "attested" language.
- Emphasize measurable controls: retention windows, audit log hashes, and verifiable runbooks rather than abstract promises.

End of doc. Use iteratively and add new objections into the master objection tracker (jira:PD-3872).
